evidence.title: WAI-ARIA 1.2 (W3C Recommendation)
evidence.what_it_decides: Defines accessibility-tree semantics (roles/states/properties of UI structure); assigns no owning implementation module.

rationale: Preserves non-collapse law: one identifier with three divergent digests does not establish a canonical owner; WAI-ARIA fixes the concept, not the owner, so unambiguous qualified identities keep copies honest.

vacancy_if_any.statement: Single-family accessibility tree operation needs a unified meaning/equality/lifecycle contract plus a named bounded-context owner before any shared-owner promotion.

rationale: Suppression semantics are corporate-internal; non-collapse law forbids electing an owner from name similarity while divergent digests leave equality unproven; qualification avoids presuming equivalence.

vacancy_if_any.statement: Requires a ratified suppression contract deciding whether alert_state or subscription_runner semantics are authoritative before imports can replace duplicates.

rationale: No external standard ranks internal display-binding ownership; two conflicting digests mean identity is ambiguous, and the non-collapse law bars canonicalization on equal names alone.

vacancy_if_any.statement: Notebook-document versus kernel-client binding responsibility must be fixed by a ratified lifecycle contract before one definition becomes canonical.

rationale: Credential-request policy is internal-corporate; non-collapse law blocks an owner verdict from repeated identifiers, and unproven digest equality forbids assuming one meaning across bridge and projection.

vacancy_if_any.statement: Needs a decided credential-scope owner plus an exact request/equality/lifecycle contract reconciling projection-side and bridge-side definitions.

rationale: Blocked proposal shows insufficient separation; non-collapse law requires decisive evidence no registry holds. Conflicting digests leave type-vs-gateway equality unproven, so qualified identities preserve safety.

vacancy_if_any.statement: Bind-membership placement between query-type definitions and gateway dispatch needs an adjudicated owner and exact contract.

rationale: Lowering-stage ownership is an internal compiler-plane choice with no external authority; distinct digests prevent presuming equivalent meanings, honoring the non-collapse law via qualification.

vacancy_if_any.statement: A decisive lowering-owner decision and unified grammar-lowering meaning/lifecycle contract are needed before any import rewriting.

evidence.title: Apache Iceberg Table Specification
evidence.what_it_decides: Fixes lakehouse table-metadata JSON and schema/partition-evolution semantics; designates no owning codec or ACL module.

rationale: Iceberg anchors the metadata domain but not module ownership; divergent SPI/ACL digests keep meaning-equality unproven, so the non-collapse law mandates unambiguous qualified identities.

vacancy_if_any.statement: Codec-SPI versus table-format-ACL translation responsibility needs an adjudicated owner and exact translate/equality/lifecycle contract before merging.

rationale: Port/adapter recording is internal payment plumbing; conflicting digests defeat canonical-owner election under the non-collapse law, so both definitions receive unique qualified identifiers pending contract proof.

vacancy_if_any.statement: Whether adapter records realize the port's single record operation must be proven by an exact equality/lifecycle contract and owner ratification.

rationale: Three provider-specific digests under one name show vendor-local variants; non-collapse law denies the name a canonical owner absent equality proofs, so per-library qualification removes ambiguity now.

vacancy_if_any.statement: Usage-event recording needs a port-canonical record contract with adapter conformance evidence replacing three private definitions.

evidence.title: METIS: serial programs for partitioning graphs, partitioning finite element meshes (Karypis Lab)
evidence.what_it_decides: Establishes graph/mesh clustering as the canonical graph-methods sense of Partition.

evidence.title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation: Table Partitioning
evidence.what_it_decides: Establishes data-layout partitioning as the distinct distributed-data sense used by exchange runtimes.

rationale: Primary sources prove two incompatible senses: graph partitioning versus data-layout partitioning. Non-collapse law's corollary—equal names never imply shared meaning—makes renaming each occurrence mandatory.

required_evidence: renamed qualified symbol ids per sense
vacancy_if_any.statement: After rename, each trait needs its own scoped identity; no further vacancy remains for cross-library owner adjudication since common ownership is disproven.

rationale: Identical digests within one runtime-resource family; conflict detail flags occurrences as provider boundaries. Non-collapse law converts repeats into imports of a family-owned backend abstraction.

required_evidence: counterexample review for both adapter candidates
vacancy_if_any.statement: Ratify a family-level TargetBackend definition above container/wasm providers, then rewrite both adapters as importers; provider-boundary code cannot own the abstraction.

evidence.title: RFC 9334: Remote ATtestation procedureS (RATS) Architecture
evidence.what_it_decides: Codifies appraisal-policy rules in attestation only, anchoring the RATS sense without covering experiment-conclusion appraisal.

rationale: RFC 9334 grounds only the RATS-family sense; identical digests across distinct families do not establish meaning-equality under the non-collapse law, so qualified identities prevent an unproven merge.

required_evidence: exact cross-family meaning/equality/lifecycle contract or divergence proof
vacancy_if_any.statement: Cross-family equivalence of AppraisalPolicy must be either proven by an exact shared meaning/equality/lifecycle contract or split by rename.

evidence.title: Apache Avro Specification: Schema Resolution
evidence.what_it_decides: Shows compatibility is parameterized per schema format/version regime, not a single portable notion.

rationale: Avro proves Compatibility is format-relative across schema-evolution, wire-codec, and envelope families; digest equality never establishes meaning, so non-collapse law requires per-family qualified identities.

vacancy_if_any.statement: Each family's compatibility predicate needs an explicit relation/equality/lifecycle contract before any shared canonical type can be proposed.

rationale: Identical digest inside one platform_commercial_support family: name-derived instability cannot elect either bound context alone, but family-level canon with adapter imports satisfies the non-collapse law.

vacancy_if_any.statement: Ratify the payment-collection contract at family scope (port-hosted), converting the Stripe adapter's copy into an import once equality and lifecycle are certified.

rationale: One analytical_method_kernels family, one identical digest, document-view semantics internal to both kernels; non-collapse law makes repeats become family-owned canonical definition plus imports.

vacancy_if_any.statement: Family ratification of a single DocumentView meaning/lifecycle contract (fields, projection equality) must precede de-duplicating classification and extraction copies.

rationale: Sealer and appraiser share experimentation_lifecycle family and byte-identical edition semantics; sealer-side sealing implies seal-once/import-elsewhere, exactly what the non-collapse law prescribes for repeats.

vacancy_if_any.statement: Adopt the sealer-hosted edition type as family canonical after certifying edition immutability/equality/lifecycle and appraiser-side import fitness.

rationale: Formula algebra and provenance families plausibly bind different node/provenance semantics; identical text proves nothing under digest-equality-is-not-meaning, so qualification preserves non-collapse until equality is proven.

vacancy_if_any.statement: Prove AST node-set and binding equality across families, or permanently split identities; owner election waits on that exact meaning contract.

rationale: 'Kernel' spans numeric compute and representation-codec senses; identical digest cannot certify shared receipt semantics across families, so non-collapse law demands qualified local identities over premature merge.

vacancy_if_any.statement: Receipt content-addressing, equality, and retention rules must be shown equivalent across facade and codec families before a canonical KernelReceipt can exist.

rationale: Occurrences span connector-wire and experimentation families despite one digest; flip-under-name-ablation confirms evidential instability, so digest-equality-is-not-meaning forces qualified identities here.

vacancy_if_any.statement: Wire-protocol editions versus experimental-protocol editions require divergence-or-equivalence proof, then owner elections per surviving sense.

rationale: Thirty-six qor kernels in a single quality_reconciliation family repeat one identical digest; refusing to pick a privileged kernel, family-shared canonical definition plus imports honors the non-collapse law.

required_evidence: family named owner decision covering all consuming kernels
vacancy_if_any.statement: Ratify one family-canonical QualityRefusal (status codes, appeal linkage, lifecycle) consumed by all thirty-six kernels via imports.
